title: When church hurts
hookLine: done with church, not with Christ: the Bible names harm done by religious people, and a bruised reed is not broken
carry: a bruised reed he will not break

lines: DONE WITH CHURCH, NOT WITH JESUS.
cards: The message arrives on a Tuesday. We've decided it's best if you step back from the worship team for now. No call.
No conversation. Or it's a sermon that seemed aimed straight at you, in front of everyone. Or a small group that stopped inviting you after the divorce.
Or something much worse, that still doesn't get said out loud. There's a short name for this. And there's a line some people say on the way out the door: I'm done with church, not with Jesus.
Today, what happens when together goes wrong.

teach.b: Church hurt. It's a modern phrase for harm done by a church or by people in it: judgment, gossip, being pushed out, being used, or abuse. The Bible doesn't pretend this can't happen.
A psalm says, in the King James Bible: "For it was not an enemy that reproached me; then I could have borne it."

It was a friend, someone the writer worshiped beside: "We took sweet counsel together, and walked unto the house of God in company." The prophets aimed some of their sharpest words at religious leaders.
Ezekiel cries: "Woe be to the shepherds of Israel that do feed themselves!"

teach.h: A BRUISED REED SHALL HE NOT BREAK.
teach.b: And when Matthew describes Jesus, he borrows a line from Isaiah: "A bruised reed shall he not break." A bruised reed is a stem already bent. He doesn't snap it.
Many Christians draw a line here that hurt people find freeing: the congregation that failed you is not the whole church, and it isn't Christ. What comes next differs from person to person.

Most churches teach that faith is meant to be lived with others, and many people who step away find a different, healthier church in time. Some need a long rest first. Being believed matters more than being argued with.

If what happened was abuse, it was not your fault, and telling someone safe outside that church matters. And if the hurt has left you somewhere dark, in the US you can call or text 988, or reach local emergency help.

how: Christians who've been hurt by a church often talk it through with a trusted friend, pastor or counselor outside that congregation; many later find a different church, and many churches now have safeguarding policies and outside reporting for abuse.

o: a split when one congregation divides in two
guilt you feel after missing a Sunday service
harm done by a church or by people in it

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.
p: harm done by a church or its people
a psalm about a friend's betrayal

s: the Bible never admits religious people can do harm
the psalms and prophets name it plainly, including leaders who "feed themselves."
"a bruised reed shall he not break" is a line from Isaiah
Matthew borrows it to describe Jesus.
if a church hurt you, it must be because you were too sensitive
being believed matters. and abuse is never the fault of the one harmed.

games.q: a friend tells you a church leader humiliated them in front of everyone, and they haven't been back since. what helps most, first?
o: defend the church; it does a lot of good.
believe them, and say you're sorry it happened.
tell them to forgive and move on.
games.why: being believed comes first. the psalm doesn't defend the friend who did the harm; it tells the truth: "it was not an enemy."

practice: If a church, or someone in one, once hurt you, let it come to mind only as far as feels safe; you don't have to relive it. Just name it, the way the psalm does, and picture setting it down beside you.
If church has only been kind to you, think of someone it wasn't kind to, and hold them gently. If you pray, you can tell God plainly what happened; if you don't, just let yourself be believed, here.

wordCard.voice: Church hurt. Harm done by a church or by people in it: real, named in the Psalms, and not the same thing as Christ.

orig.note: Greek: a bruised, crushed reed (Matthew 12:20), borrowing Isaiah 42:3.

carryVoice: Your line: a bruised reed he will not break. Bent is not the same as broken. Day one hundred forty-three.
